[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard defines the mandatory structure, content requirements, and quality rules for work items that are intended for autonomous AI agent execution. Any issue, ticket, or work item that will trigger an AI agent pipeline MUST conform to this standard before the agent dispatch label is applied. The standard exists to ensure that agents receive complete, unambiguous, parseable context — because agent output quality is directly and entirely determined by the quality of the specification the agent receives.
page_texts.5:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#scope]

### Scope

**In scope:**
- All work items labeled or designated for autonomous AI agent execution regardless of the issue tracker platform used
- Issue tracker templates used to author agent-executable specifications
- Validation gate logic that checks compliance with this standard before agent dispatch

**Out of scope:**
- Human-only work items not intended for agent execution
- Internally generated sub-tasks created by an agent during execution
- Post-execution PR review criteria (governed by ADR-GOV-008 and STD-GOV-AI-003)
page_texts.6:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory.** No agent pipeline MUST invoke an AI agent against a work item that has not passed structural validation confirming compliance with this standard. The validation gate implementing this check MUST fail closed — agent invocation is blocked, not warned, on non-compliance.
page_texts.7:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

AI agents cannot resolve ambiguity through experience, domain knowledge, or conversation the way human engineers do. An imprecise specification passed to an agent is not a starting point for negotiation — it is the complete and final input context. Inconsistently structured specifications produce inconsistent agent output, requiring human rework that negates the productivity benefit of autonomous execution. This standard enforces the minimum specification quality required for reliable agent output, protecting the investment in agent pipeline infrastructure and the engineering time that reviews agent-produced pull requests.

page_texts.9:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

Every agent-executable work item MUST include all four of the following required sections, populated with compliant content. The presence of section headers without substantive content does NOT constitute compliance.

**REQ-001 — Goal Section**: The work item MUST contain a `## Goal` section with exactly one sentence that:
- Names the specific component, file, system, or bounded scope of the task
- Uses an imperative action verb (Add, Update, Remove, Generate, Implement, Migrate, Refactor)
- Defines a scope boundary that an agent can use to determine when it has exceeded its mandate
- Does NOT contain multiple clauses, business outcome statements, or questions

**REQ-002 — Acceptance Criteria Section**: The work item MUST contain a `## Acceptance Criteria` section with:
- A minimum of two independently verifiable, checkable items
- Each criterion stated as an output state, not a process step
- At least one criterion that references a testable technical outcome (test coverage threshold, lint result, validation output, schema conformance)
- No criterion that requires human judgment to evaluate (e.g., "code is clean," "output looks good")

**REQ-003 — Constraints Section**: The work item MUST contain a `## Constraints` section with:
- A minimum of two explicit constraint references
- At least one reference to a specific, locatable standards document, pattern identifier, or enterprise guideline (section and document, not generic terms)
- At least one explicit scope boundary defining the target files, components, or system boundaries
- No generic or unverifiable constraints (e.g., "follow best practices," "be secure")

**REQ-004 — Enterprise Work Item Reference**: The work item MUST contain a `## Enterprise Work Item` section with a valid, non-empty cross-reference to the governing work item in the enterprise work management system, following the format defined in STD-GOV-AI-003.
page_texts.10:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- **REP-001**: Limit the Constraints section to the constraints that are genuinely material to the task — an exhaustive list of every tangentially applicable standard reduces agent context quality by diluting the most relevant references
- **REP-002**: Write acceptance criteria in the past tense ("Rate limiting is applied...") rather than as instructions ("Apply rate limiting...") — past-tense criteria are more naturally evaluated as completion checks
- **REP-003**: Include a `Do not modify:` constraint line naming any files or components that must not be altered by the agent, to prevent unintended scope expansion
- **REP-004**: Have a peer (engineer or product owner) review the spec before applying the dispatch label — the spec review is as important as the PR review
page_texts.11:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- **PRO-001**: A work item MUST NOT have the agent dispatch label applied while any required section is absent, empty, or contains only placeholder text
- **PRO-002**: The Goal section MUST NOT contain multiple sentences, compound clauses joined by "and," or business outcome language that does not define a technical scope boundary
- **PRO-003**: Acceptance criteria MUST NOT include process-level items ("Create a PR," "Run the tests," "Ask for review") — only output state items
- **PRO-004**: The Constraints section MUST NOT contain references to documents or sections that do not exist in the repository or enterprise knowledge base accessible to the agent
- **PRO-005**: Work items MUST NOT contain Protected Health Information (PHI), Personally Identifiable Information (PII), security credentials, tokens, or connection strings in any section — the issue tracker is the execution surface only, not a regulated data store
page_texts.12:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. A team lead may request a temporary exception for a specific work item by submitting a request to the Enterprise Architecture Practice with justification and a remediation plan
2. Exceptions are approved for a maximum of one sprint and require documentation of why the standard cannot be met and what manual mitigations are in place
3. Systemic exceptions (a team consistently unable to meet a specific requirement) must be escalated to the EA Practice for standard revision rather than repeated individual exception grants
4. All exceptions must be logged in the governance record associated with the originating enterprise work item

page_texts.15:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#spec-section-detection]

#### Spec Section Detection

A compliant validation gate implementation MUST detect all four required sections using header-based matching. Section detection rules:

| Section | Required Header (exact) | Minimum Content Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Goal | `## Goal` | One non-empty line of text following the header (excluding blank lines and HTML comments) |
| Acceptance Criteria | `## Acceptance Criteria` | Minimum two lines beginning with `- [ ]` |
| Constraints | `## Constraints` | Minimum two lines beginning with `-` |
| Enterprise Work Item | `## Enterprise Work Item` | One line matching the enterprise cross-reference regex defined in STD-GOV-AI-003 |
page_texts.16:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#goal-sentence-validation]

#### Goal Sentence Validation

The validation gate SHOULD enforce the following rules on the Goal section content:
- Content between `## Goal` and the next `##` header contains exactly one sentence (one terminal punctuation mark)
- Content does not begin with "As a" (user story format — not a valid goal sentence)
- Content does not end with `?` (not a question)
page_texts.17:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#acceptance-criteria-validation]

#### Acceptance Criteria Validation

The validation gate MUST enforce:
- A minimum of two `- [ ]` checklist items following the `## Acceptance Criteria` header
- No `- [ ]` item whose text is identical to a template placeholder (e.g., contains only whitespace or matches the template default text)
page_texts.18:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#constraints-validation]

#### Constraints Validation

The validation gate MUST enforce:
- A minimum of two `-` list items following the `## Constraints` header
- At least one item beginning with `Follow:` or `Target:` (the mandatory constraint types defined by PTN-APP-GOV-005)
page_texts.19:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#architecture-constraints]

### Architecture Constraints

- The validation gate is an atomic, independent pipeline stage — it MUST run before any agent context assembly or invocation begins
- The validation gate MUST run in under 60 seconds — excessive validation latency creates a poor authoring feedback loop
- Validation logic MUST be stored as version-controlled code, not embedded in platform UI configuration, so that validation rules evolve with the standard
- The validation gate MUST post a machine-generated corrective comment on the work item on failure, identifying each non-compliant element by name with the remediation action required
page_texts.21:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#issue-tracker-template-configuration]

#### Issue Tracker Template Configuration

The agent-executable spec template MUST be deployed as a native issue tracker template (e.g., `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agent-task.md` for GitHub-based repositories). The template MUST pre-populate section headers and include HTML comments providing authoring guidance within each section.

**Minimum required template structure:**

```markdown
---
name: Agent Task
about: Specification for an autonomous AI agent execution task
title: "[AGENT] "
labels: agent-task
assignees: ''
---

## Goal

<!-- One sentence. What should the agent accomplish? Name the specific component or scope. Use an imperative verb: Add, Update, Remove, Generate, Implement. -->


## Acceptance Criteria

<!-- Minimum two checkable items. State each as an output condition, not a process step. Include at least one testable technical outcome. -->

- [ ]
- [ ]

## Constraints

<!-- Minimum two explicit references. At minimum: a standards document reference (section and document) and a target scope. No generic statements. -->

- Follow:
- Target:

## Enterprise Work Item

<!-- Required. Cross-reference to the governing work item. Format per STD-GOV-AI-003. Example: WI#4821 -->

WI#
```
page_texts.22:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#validation-gate-configuration]

#### Validation Gate Configuration

```yaml
# Minimum validation gate configuration
validation:
  goal:
    required: true
    min_sentences: 1
    max_sentences: 1
  acceptance_criteria:
    required: true
    min_items: 2
    item_format: "- [ ]"
  constraints:
    required: true
    min_items: 2
  enterprise_work_item:
    required: true
    format_regex: "(WI|AB|PROJ)#[0-9A-Z-]+"  # Customize per enterprise platform
  on_failure:
    action: "comment_and_halt"
    remove_trigger_label: true
```

page_texts.25:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#phase-1-template-deployment]

#### Phase 1: Template Deployment

1. Deploy the agent-task issue template to the repository's issue tracker template directory
2. Configure the template as the default for issues with the `agent-task` label (if the platform supports label-gating of templates)
3. Publish the spec authoring guide as a companion document in the team's wiki or repository documentation
4. Run an authoring workshop with engineers and product owners using before/after spec examples — one well-formed spec and one anti-pattern spec
page_texts.26:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#phase-2-validation-gate-deployment]

#### Phase 2: Validation Gate Deployment

1. Implement the spec structural validation workflow as the first, independent stage of the agent dispatch pipeline (PTN-TEC-AI-002)
2. Configure the enterprise work item cross-reference regex to match the format used by the team's enterprise work management platform (per STD-GOV-AI-003)
3. Implement the corrective comment template — the comment must name each failing requirement and the specific action to remediate it
4. Test the gate with: (a) a fully compliant spec, (b) each individual missing section, (c) a spec with a missing enterprise work item reference
page_texts.27:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#phase-3-pilot-and-calibration]

#### Phase 3: Pilot and Calibration

1. Run 5–10 agent tasks manually (without automated dispatch) using compliant specs to validate that the spec format produces reliable agent output before automating the pipeline
2. Track validation failure rate from the first sprint of automated dispatch — a failure rate above 20% indicates the authoring standard needs reinforcement or the template needs improvement
3. Review failed specs in the first sprint retrospective and identify the most common failure modes for targeted authoring guidance improvement
page_texts.28:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| Template deployed | Agent-task template available in issue tracker | Issue creation flow presents template | Screenshot or template file presence |
| Validation gate active | Gate blocks agent on non-compliant spec | Create test issue with missing section; confirm agent does not fire | Pipeline run log showing halt + comment |
| Corrective comment accuracy | Failed validation comment names missing elements | Review comment content on a test failure | Comment text matches non-compliant elements |
| Enterprise link enforced | Gate blocks dispatch without valid WI# | Create test issue without WI#; confirm halt | Pipeline run log |
| PHI prohibition | Issue tracker access controls prevent external data entry | Access control review | Access control configuration |
page_texts.29:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#testing-requirements]

### Testing Requirements

- **Unit Testing**: Validate the spec parsing logic against a suite of compliant and non-compliant spec fixtures, covering every individual failure case
- **Integration Testing**: Validate end-to-end pipeline behavior — a compliant spec triggers agent dispatch; each individual non-compliance variant halts with the correct comment
- **Regression Testing**: Re-run the full suite whenever the validation gate logic or the standard requirements are updated
- **Authoring Testing**: Run a structured exercise with 3+ team members authoring a spec without assistance; rate each spec for compliance and use failures to improve the template
page_texts.30:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#documentation-requirements]

### Documentation Requirements

- The spec authoring guide MUST be published and linked from the agent-task issue template description
- The validation gate failure comment MUST link to this standard for remediation reference
- Each team deploying the agent pipeline MUST document the enterprise work item cross-reference format they are using in their local runbook

---
page_texts.33:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#assessment-criteria]

#### Assessment Criteria

- **Template Deployed**: The agent-task issue template exists in the repository and matches the minimum required structure defined in this standard
- **Validation Gate Active**: The spec validation stage is present and configured as the first stage of the agent dispatch pipeline, and it fails closed on non-compliance
- **Zero PHI in Specs**: No issue tracker content contains PHI, PII, credentials, or non-public regulated data
- **100% Enterprise Link Coverage**: All agent-executed issues (those that produced a PR) contain a valid enterprise work item cross-reference
page_texts.34:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#assessment-process]

#### Assessment Process

1. Quarterly compliance review by Engineering Lead using the validation criteria table above
2. Annual standard review by Enterprise Architecture Practice to assess whether requirements remain appropriate as agent capabilities and tooling evolve
3. Incident-triggered review whenever an agent pipeline is found to have executed against a non-compliant spec
page_texts.35:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#monitoring-requirements]

### Monitoring Requirements

- **Validation Failure Rate**: Track the percentage of `agent-task` issues that fail validation each sprint; report to engineering lead monthly; escalate if rate exceeds 15% in two consecutive sprints
- **Spec Quality Trend**: Track PR pass rate for agent-produced PRs (agent PRs that pass all branch protection gates on first submission) as a downstream proxy for spec quality
- **Template Drift**: Alert when the deployed issue template diverges from the minimum structure defined in this standard (detected via template content hash comparison in CI)
page_texts.37:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#exception-categories]

#### Exception Categories

- **Temporary Exception**: A specific high-priority task requires agent execution but cannot fully meet REQ-003 (Constraints) because the applicable standard does not yet exist. Approved for maximum one sprint with a documented commitment to author the missing standard.
- **Permanent Exception**: A specific team workflow produces work items in a format that structurally cannot accommodate the template (e.g., an external ticketing system with no markdown body support). Requires EA Practice approval and a documented compensating control.
page_texts.38:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#exception-management-process]

#### Exception Management Process

1. Submit exception request to EA Practice with: the work item ID, the specific requirement that cannot be met, the business justification, and the proposed compensating control
2. EA Practice reviews within 5 business days; escalates to Architecture Review Board if the exception sets a precedent
3. Approved exceptions are documented in the governance record and reviewed at the next quarterly compliance assessment
page_texts.39:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Architecture Practice — responsible for standard maintenance and version updates
- **Compliance Monitor**: Engineering Lead per team — tracks validation failure rate and spec quality metrics
- **Governance Body**: Architecture Review Board — reviews systemic exceptions and approves major standard revisions
- **Subject Matter Experts**: Platform Engineering Team — provides technical guidance on validation gate implementation

page_texts.42:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#example-1-compliant-implementation-spec]

#### Example 1: Compliant Implementation Spec

**Context:** Implementing rate limiting middleware on an API gateway component

**Compliant spec:**

```markdown
## Goal
Add request rate limiting middleware to the API gateway to prevent abuse of public-facing endpoints.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rate limiting middleware added to components/api-gateway/src/middleware/rate-limiter/
- [ ] Default limit of 100 requests per minute per client IP, configurable via environment variable
- [ ] Unit tests achieve ≥ 90% branch coverage on rate-limiting logic
- [ ] Standards/application/api-standards.md § 4.2 Rate Limiting requirements satisfied
- [ ] Existing auth middleware unit tests continue to pass (no regression)

## Constraints
- Follow: standards/application/api-standards.md § 4.2 Rate Limiting
- Follow: patterns/application/api-microservices/ middleware patterns
- Target: components/api-gateway/src/middleware/
- Do not modify: components/api-gateway/src/auth/

## Enterprise Work Item
WI#4821
```

**Compliance Evidence:** All four required sections present; Goal is one bounded imperative sentence; five checkable criteria including one technical threshold; two explicit standards references plus scope boundary and exclusion; WI# present.
page_texts.43:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-001-agent-executable-work-item-specification-standard.md#example-2-anti-pattern--non-compliant-spec]

#### Example 2: Anti-Pattern — Non-Compliant Spec

**Context:** Same task, authored without applying this standard

```markdown
## Goal
Improve the API gateway and make it more secure and reliable with rate limiting and better error handling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Code is clean and well-tested
- [ ] Rate limiting works

## Constraints
- Follow best practices
- Be secure

## Enterprise Work Item
(TBD)
```

**Non-compliance findings:**
- REQ-001: Goal contains multiple clauses ("and make it more secure and reliable with rate limiting and better error handling") — not a single bounded sentence
- REQ-002: "Code is clean" is not independently verifiable; "Rate limiting works" has no measurable criterion; fewer than two criteria reference a testable technical outcome
- REQ-003: "Follow best practices" and "Be secure" are generic — no specific document or section referenced; no target scope defined
- REQ-004: Enterprise work item reference is absent ("TBD" does not match the required format)
